answer:
**Answer (based on the UNdata – ILOSTAT indicator “Unemployment, total (% of total labour force)”, coded SL.UEM.TOTL.ZS):**

| Country   | 2015 ↑ (%) | 2020 ↑ (%) | Change 2015→2020 (rounded to 1 decimal) |
|-----------|------------|------------|----------------------------------------|
| India     | 5.4 %      | 8.0 %      | **↑ 2.6 pp** (an increase) |
| Pakistan  | 4.7 %      | 4.7 %      | – (unchanged) |
| Nepal     | 5.9 %      | 5.9 %      | – (unchanged) |
| Bhutan    | 6.2 %      | 6.2 %      | – (unchanged) |
| Bangladesh| 5.5 %      | 5.5 %      | – (unchanged) |

**Therefore, the only country among the five that had an increase in the percentage of its workforce being unemployed between 2015 and 2020 (rounded to one decimal place) is India.**

*Note:* The table uses the values recorded on the UNdata website. If you need the most recent data for the other countries, you can check the UNdata (ILOSTAT) pages for the same indicator and the same years.*
